exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Here is how a strong planner explains a different event — a school field day — so you can see the moves, not the answers.

traits.sample: I found the greatest common factor of 18 water bottles and 24 granola bars. Using 6 packs uses every item and gives each pack the same number of each item.
traits.why: Naming GCF and saying what it does shows the skill, which earns 'correct with explanation' on the rubric.

traits.sample: I made 6 packs because 6 is the biggest number that divides both 18 and 24 with nothing left over.
traits.why: The 'because' proves the number was reasoned, not guessed.

traits.trait: Connects math to the real decision
traits.sample: My total cost was $52.50 for 15 players, so each player costs $3.50. Compared with the stated $60 ceiling, $7.50 remains.
traits.why: Linking division to a real budget decision shows the math matters, which top rubric rows reward.

traits.sample: I estimated about $4 per player before dividing, and $3.50 is close to that, so my decimal work makes sense.
traits.why: An estimate check catches decimal mistakes and shows expert-level number sense.
